name: Rally allies
summary: A unit makes the teammates around it fight better for a while: they fire faster, hit harder, move faster or take less damage. It comes as an always-on aura around the carrier, as a timed call on a key that covers everyone near the caller, or as a buff placed on a chosen area. The buffer itself is usually a modest fighter, or pays for the effect with a cooldown, money, a charge earned in combat or even a spent minion. It has to stay close to the units it lifts, so it is the first thing the enemy wants dead. The levers are which stat is raised, the radius, how long it lasts, whether the buffer gets the boost too and whether several buffs add up.
counterplay: Kill or drive off the buffer first: the boost ends with it, and many buffers (officers, casters, thralls) are fragile. Where the aura rides on a heavy unit, cut it off from the group it lifts or wait out its call.
Wait out a timed call: back off for its few seconds and come back while it is on cooldown.
Fight the group outside the ring: catch stragglers, or pull the allies away from the buffer so they leave its radius.
Splash the clump: an aura draws teammates into one tight group.
Switch the aura off or block it where the game allows: in Overwatch a hacked Lúcio loses his aura, and in Tempest Rising infantry under Subjugation can't receive buffs at all.
Against an armour aura, change the kind of hit: a flat cut to each ranged shot does little against heavy single hits or melee.

other_examples.note: A costly one-man officer who can fight but is fielded to lift the British infantry around him: every squad inside his command radius fights better, and the bonus grows as he gains rank from kills made near him. He can be told to shadow one squad so it never drops out of the radius, and once he has a rank he gets a timed call that briefly raises attack and defence and shrugs off suppression. Only three may be fielded, and several on one group stack only in part.

An armour rally on a key: for a block of energy the Sentry raises a bubble around itself for a short time, and friendly units inside lose a small fixed amount from every ranged hit they take. The wiki's lore text adds that so wide a field is too thin to matter much against heavy ordnance.

sources.title: Guardian Shield, StarCraft Wiki
sources.note: Its Game Effect box (the wiki template SC2SentryShield) gives the energy cost, the radius, the duration and the fixed cut to ranged damage.

other_examples.unit: Commissar Lord: Lead by Example (Imperial Guard)
other_examples.note: A call that grows while the caller fights: for a short time the hero moves faster, allied infantry around him deal a little more damage, and every blow he lands adds that bonus once more. It costs energy, needs a piece of wargear and then waits out a cooldown.

sources.title: Retribution/Lead by Example, Dawn of War Wiki

other_examples.note: The attached-leader form: an infantry commander who joins one Guardsmen squad and raises that squad's morale and health regeneration for as long as he stays with it.

sources.title: Dark Crusade/Commissar, Dawn of War Wiki

other_examples.unit: Comms field (GDF Comms Officer, Comms Rig and others)
other_examples.note: The GDF's standing aura: the Comms Officer, the Comms Rig while in its Comms mode, the Drone Command Unit, the Air Control Tower and the Support Beacon each give off a field, and friendly units inside it shoot and move faster. It is always on, and doctrines widen the field, toughen its providers or hand the bonus to every infantryman.

sources.title: Ability, Tempest Rising Wiki
sources.note: Lists the Comms perk with each provider's field radius.

shooter_analogues.note: A backpack banner that turns damage dealt into a team call. Hurting enemies fills a rage meter; when it is full the Soldier sounds a bugle, and for a short time every hit by a teammate standing within a set distance of him, his own hits too, lands as a mini-crit. Buffed players glow with rings at their feet, the meter empties if he dies, and he can hold the call back for the right moment.

sources.title: Buff Banner, Official Team Fortress Wiki

shooter_analogues.unit: Lúcio: Crossfade and Amp It Up
shooter_analogues.note: An always-on aura around the hero that he flips between two songs with one key: one heals the allies near him, the other speeds them up. It needs a clear line to each ally and lingers for a moment when they step out. A second key turns the current song up for a few seconds, and being hacked switches the aura off.

sources.title: Lúcio, Overwatch Wiki
sources.note: Each ability box has an official_description field next to the wiki's own details.

shooter_analogues.note: A rally laid down as a lane: the ultimate sends a spirit fox running ahead, and allies who stay in the lane behind it move, shoot and reload faster and get their cooldowns back sooner. The boost drops off a moment after they leave the lane.

sources.title: Kiriko, Overwatch Wiki
sources.note: The ability box has an official_description field next to the wiki's own details.

player_translation.summary: A buffer player makes the teammates around them stronger: a ring that follows the unit, or a call on a key that gives everyone inside the ring a few seconds of faster fire, faster movement or tougher armour. The unit is worth more than its own gun, so both teams fight over where it stands.
as_user: You buy a unit with a modest weapon whose real value is the ring around it: teammates inside fire faster, move faster or take less damage.
With the timed call you pick the moment: press Q as your team's push starts or as the enemy commits, the ring flares for a few seconds, and then you wait out the cooldown.
Positioning is the job: stay inside the group you lift but behind its front, and move with it. A buffer who dies first wasted the pick.
You get assist score for what your buffed teammates do, and your HUD counts how many allies stand in the ring.
Variants ask for more: earn the call by dealing damage, pay team money for a buff placed at range, or flip the aura between two effects.
as_target: You see the ring on the ground and a marker on every buffed enemy, so you know who is boosted and from where.
Kill or push away the buffer and the boost ends, at once or after a moment.
Against a timed call, back off for its few seconds and return while it is on cooldown.
The ring pulls enemies together, so splash and area weapons pay off.
teammates: Allies gather on the buffer before a push and ask for the boost with a ping; the buffer answers when the call is ready.
Two buffers of different kinds, such as speed and armour, add up to a strong push; two of the same kind should not.
Keeping the buffer alive is a team task: front-liners screen it, and it follows them.
On the enemy side, snipers and flankers get a clear target, and a disabler who can silence the buffer shuts the ring off.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; the aura itself needs no key.
Q fires the timed call around you: the ring flashes and the cooldown starts.
For the placed version, hold Q to show a target circle at the cursor and release to buff that area.
Middle mouse, the universal ping: teammates ask for a boost here, and the buffer answers that it is coming.
feedback: A team-coloured ring on the ground around the buffer, brighter while a call is active and visible to both teams.
Buffed units carry a small marker at their feet or a tint on their weapon, with an icon and a timer on their own HUD.
A horn, a shout or a loudspeaker when the call starts, and a softer sound when it ends.
The buffer's HUD shows the allies in the ring and the cooldown or charge.
changes_from_rts: RTS auras are passive and the army sits in them without thinking; a player needs something to do, so the timed call on a key is the default and a passive aura stays weak.
In an RTS the buffed units belong to the same player; here they are other players, so the buffer needs assist score and the receivers need to see who is boosting them.
Tempest Rising's Line Officer lifts infantry only. Limits by class work as variants, but the default should lift every teammate so the pick is never dead.
Generals does not let several propaganda towers add up; keep that rule so a team can't pile identical buffers onto one push.
RTS buffs can be large (the Line Officer's troops move and fire half again as fast). In a shooter, where aim already swings fights, keep the numbers smaller and the windows short.

team_play.notes: The buffer is strong only through others, and the others are stronger around it, so the team groups up and screens it while the enemy coordinates to kill it first or to wait out its call. No hook names a pure buff: protector covers the armour auras, escort-dependency the buffer's need for a screen.

notes: A radius check that puts timed stat modifiers on allies; the stats it touches (fire rate, speed, damage taken) must already be adjustable per unit.
Stacking rules: same buffs don't add up, different ones do, and one cap on the total.
Ring, markers and HUD icons for both teams, and assist scoring for the buffer.
Variants add a charge meter fed by damage, a targeted area, or a toggle between two auras.
A buff multiplies the strongest unit on the team, so each buffed pairing has to be balanced, not just the buffer.
Stacked buffers can snowball a push; cap the total boost and stop identical buffs adding up.
A passive aura strong enough to matter becomes a must-pick that is dull to play; one too weak is never bought.
Fire-rate and speed boosts change how fights feel for the enemy more than armour does; start with small numbers.
Enemies must be able to tell who is buffed and by whom, or damage numbers seem to lie.
Several rings and markers in one brawl clutter a top-down view; keep one ring style per team and thin markers.
A call that starts off screen needs a sound the enemy can hear.

variants.name: Timed call
variants.summary: Press a key and everyone near you gets a short, strong boost; then the call is on cooldown. The default for a player unit.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Line Officer (Inspire Troops); Company of Heroes Lieutenant (Heroic Charge)

variants.name: Standing aura
variants.summary: An always-on ring around the unit gives a small boost to whoever stands in it, with no key to press.
variants.seen_in: Generals Overlord with a Propaganda Tower; Company of Heroes Lieutenant; Tempest Rising Comms field; Overwatch Lúcio

variants.name: Ward
variants.summary: The boost is protection: allies inside take less damage, either a share off everything or a fixed cut to each ranged hit that blunts small arms more than heavy guns.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Sentry (Guardian Shield); Tempest Rising Consecration

variants.name: Earned call
variants.summary: The call has no cooldown; a meter fills as the buffer deals damage and empties on death, so only a buffer who fights gets to rally.

variants.name: Placed blessing
variants.summary: The buff is put on a chosen area at range and covers whoever stands there, not the caster; each use costs team money or another price and has a long wait.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Vimana (Sacrificial Benediction, paid in credits) and Enlightened (Sacrifice, paid with the unit)

variants.name: Two songs
variants.summary: One aura with two settings, such as speed or healing; a key flips between them, and a second key turns the current one up for a moment.

variants.name: Shadow one ally
variants.summary: The buffer ties itself to one teammate or squad and follows it, so that ally is always inside the bonus; the rest of the team gets less.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes Lieutenant (Maintain Command Range); Dawn of War Commissar attached to a squad

variants.name: Growing call
variants.summary: The call starts small and grows with every hit the caller lands while it runs, so the buffer has to fight at the front to make it count.
variants.seen_in: Dawn of War II: Retribution Commissar Lord (Lead by Example)

variants.name: Rally lane
variants.summary: The buff is a lane drawn forward from the caster: allies who run down it move, fire and recover faster, and lose the boost when they leave it.

adds_strengths.why: Teammates near it fire faster, move faster or take less damage, so a group with it beats the same group without it.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its worth lies in others: alone it is a modest fighter, and it has to stand close to the group it lifts, where splash and snipers find it.

countered_by.why: Snipers pick the buffer out of the group, and the boost ends with it.
Flankers get behind the front line to the buffer standing just inside it.
The ring pulls teammates into one clump that area damage hits all at once.

open_questions: Should the default be a timed call on a key, with the passive aura kept as the weaker variant?
Which stats may a rally touch in Shamble Frontlines: fire rate, speed, damage taken, accuracy? Accuracy only matters if weapons have spread.
Do buffs from different buffers add up, and is there a cap on the total boost one unit can carry?
Does the buffer get its own buff, or only the teammates around it?
How much score does the buffer earn for what its buffed teammates do, so that the pick is rewarding?
Should some enemy effect block buffs, as Subjugation does for infantry in Tempest Rising?

The word lists make any call charged by a meter an ultimate, which starts at t3, so the earned call can't appear on a cheap unit, although Team Fortress 2 hands its Buff Banner to an ordinary class. Should a meter-fed call be allowed below t3? That would be a change to the word lists.

shooter_fit.reason: Proven in team shooters (the Buff Banner, Lúcio's aura), and a ring on the ground reads well from above. It gives the team a reason to group up and the enemy a target, but a purely passive aura is dull to play, so the timed call should lead.
